comparison: Both evaluate the primary genome-wide GLMM finding (C3, C21-C23). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the statistical approach appropriate and gene set enrichment robust. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging importance but raising critical concerns about potential confounding from systematic expression differences between tumor classes and requesting within-cancer-type validation.

Both evaluate cell line validation in CCLE (C45-C48). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding replication of expression patterns and protein abundance validation strengthen findings, with cell-autonomous inference reasonable. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, raising methodological concerns about different model architectures between TCGA and CCLE analyses and questioning whether cancer type confounding was properly addressed.

Both evaluate shRNA perturbation experiments (C49-C53). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the data establishes causality with appropriate specificity and robustness via jackknife resampling. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, directly challenging generalizability claims and stating that leave-one-out analysis would not reveal if signal was driven by a small subset of cancer types, requesting individual cancer type analyses.

Both evaluate systematic drug screening (C58-C59). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding that most drugs showing no effect establishes specificity while identification of effective drug categories provides translational relevance. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED with no specific concerns raised about these findings.

Both evaluate drug screening validation (C54-C57). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding PRISM data provides independent validation with strong evidence from proteasome inhibitors. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, with editor noting solid evidence for the association and drug data supporting causal interpretation.

Both evaluate alternative splicing analysis (C28-C32). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding appropriate controls for eQTL effects and robustness analysis strengthens conclusions, though causal direction is inferential. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, expressing significant skepticism about the weak effect and questioning why different splicing events should respond uniformly, suggesting potential common confounder.

Both evaluate mutation type correlation analysis (C17-C19). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding correlation analysis clearly presented and justifying methodological choice to aggregate protein-coding mutations. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, not challenging this descriptive finding that serves as methodological justification.

Both evaluate proteostasis response characterization (C33-C40) and robustness analyses (C41-C43). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for both, finding detailed characterization well-documented and validation analyses strengthen findings. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging solid evidence but raising concerns that jackknife analysis would not reveal subset-driven signals and requesting true within-cancer-type analyses with specific genes.

OpenEval evaluates validation analyses (C41-C44) as SUPPORTED, finding jackknife resampling, within-cancer-type analysis, and age stratification support robustness. Peer reviewers evaluate overlapping robustness claims (C41-C43) as UNCERTAIN, noting jackknife would not reveal if signal was driven by small subset of cancer types and requesting more granular within-cancer-type analyses.

OpenEval rates the theoretical framework (C1-C15) as SUPPORTED, finding evolutionary principles and empirical findings establish sound logic connecting lack of recombination to mutational load accumulation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these foundational theoretical claims.

OpenEval rates the synthesized mechanistic model (C60-C71) as SUPPORTED, finding mechanisms well-supported by citations and mitigation strategies directly supported by study data, though some aspects remain speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this synthesis section.

OpenEval rates evolutionary implications and compensatory mechanisms (C72-C76) as UNCERTAIN, finding indirect selection inference logical but specific mechanisms speculative and whole genome duplication paradox unresolved. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these evolutionary speculation claims.

OpenEval rates therapeutic implications (C77-C83) as SUPPORTED, finding inference about proteostasis vulnerabilities well-supported by perturbation and drug data with proper citations for clinical use. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these therapeutic discussion claims.

OpenEval rates connections to aging biology (C84-C88) as SUPPORTED, finding parallels well-supported by citations and identification of strategic differences properly documented. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these aging biology connections.
